facts.claim: 1959년 TMRC 사전이 hack · hacker 를 실음
facts.note: The MIT Tech Model Railroad Club Dictionary defined hack in 1959 (not yet in a computer context) as ... and "hacker" was defined as "one who hacks, or makes them".

facts.claim: 동아리가 DEC PDP-1 을 쓰며 은어가 컴퓨터 문화로
facts.note: Much of TMRC's jargon was later imported into early computing culture, because the club started using a DEC PDP-1 and applied its local model railroad slang in this computing context.

facts.claim: 1983년 언론이 414s 사건 범인들을 해커라 부르면서 오용에 대한 불만 시작
facts.note: Complaints about supposed mainstream misuse started as early as 1983, when media used "hacker" to refer to the computer criminals involved in The 414s case.

facts.claim: 1963년 MIT 학생 신문 The Tech 가 전화망을 건드리는 사람에게 나쁜 뜻으로 씀
facts.note: An article from MIT's student paper The Tech used the term hacker in this context already in 1963 in its pejorative meaning for someone messing with the phone system.

question.hintNote: The hacker ethics were chronicled by Steven Levy in Hackers: Heroes of the Computer Revolution ... Hacker ethics are concerned primarily with sharing, openness, collaboration, and engaging in the hands-on imperative.
